children: The WASDE report showed some changes to U.S. corn and soybean production and yields, which sparked some selling of futures in afternoon trading. But the lasting impact of the WASDE isn't expected to linger long in the minds of grain traders, says the Hightower Report in a note. "Without a surprise in this report, the market will quickly return to trading other fundamentals such as South American weather and China demand, which has been very strong this week," says the firm in a note, in reference to soybean market conditions. Rallying in corn futures is also not expected to rally much on the report's data. CBOT corn is now down 0.5%, while soybeans fall 2.4% and wheat sheds 2.4%. (kirk.maltais@wsj.com)
